title: Vintage Gibson SG Standard Value Guide: Eras And Wear
description: Assess vintage Gibson SG Standard value by era, pickups, finish and repair history. Joe explains what separates collector examples from changed guitars.
h1: Vintage Gibson SG Standard Value Guide
alt: Cherry SG Standard body with two humbuckers, four knobs and a sideways vibrato in a red-lined case

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Gibson SG Standard Worth?
faqs.a: A clean, all-original cherry 1965 Gibson SG Standard with its original case sits around $12,000 to $14,000 in the completed-sale comparisons reviewed as of October 2026. I use that band for the small-guard, Maestro-equipped guitar with normal light wear and no structural repairs.

faqs.q: What Condition Does This Price Range Assume?
faqs.a: Clean, all-original examples with original case and no structural repairs; normal light wear accepted. Comparable seller grades range from Very Good to Excellent. I match those details before using the $12,000 to $14,000 range for an individual guitar.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Published Range?
faqs.a: It isn't. The table describes completed-sale comparisons before shipping and tax. A buying offer also accounts for the instrument's condition, selling costs, preparation and the dealer's margin. I explain an offer for the actual guitar rather than promising the top of a general range.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Collector Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original guitar. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping is a separate alteration.
